key_insight: Constraint-aware reinforcement learning reduces battery sizing needs for PV ramp-rate smoothing while maintaining grid-code compliance.
engineering_relevance: Jointly designing battery capacity and control can reduce storage requirements for integrating variable solar generation into the grid.
method: Learn a causal state-feedback policy from historical PV data without requiring forecasts during deployment.
Restrict battery actions to a feasibility interval incorporating ramp-rate, converter-power, and state-of-charge constraints.
Use full-horizon input-convex neural network optimization as a noncausal benchmark for minimum battery requirements.
evidence_signal: Across three real-world PV datasets at a 10%/min ramp-rate limit, CARL reduced peak battery power by 8.7–10.4% and energy capacity by 47.5–62.6% versus conventional ramp-rate control while maintaining compliance.
watch_item: Generalization to unseen PV variability and real-world battery behavior requires further validation beyond the reported datasets.
paper_title: Battery Energy Storage Sizing in PV Ramp-Rate Smoothing using Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Based Controller
